etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Middle French texture, borrowed from Latin textūra (“a weaving, web, texture, structure”), from textus, past participle of texere (“to weave”). See text. Doublet of tessitura.

definitions.definition: The feel or shape of a surface or substance; the smoothness, roughness, softness, etc. of something.
(art) The quality given to a work of art by the composition and interaction of its parts.
(computer graphics) An image applied to a polygon to create the appearance of a surface.

quote.citation: 2004, Will Smith, Maximum PC Guide to Building a Dream PC (page 97)
quote.text: The videocard is responsible for drawing every polygon, texture, and particle effect in every game you play.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) The act or art of weaving.

quote.citation: 1650, Thomas Browne, Pseudodoxia Epidemica: […], 2nd edition, London:  […]  A[braham] Miller, for Edw[ard] Dod and Nath[aniel] Ekins, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Skins, although a natural habit unto all before the invention of texture, was something more unto Adam.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) Something woven; a woven fabric; a web.

quote.citation: a. 1749 (date written), James Thomson, “Spring”, in The Seasons, London:  […]  A[ndrew] Millar, and sold by Thomas Cadell, […], published 1768, →OCLC:
quote.text: Others, apart far in the grassy dale, / Or roughening waste, their humble texture weave.

definitions.definition: To create or apply a texture.
